answer: A stake-weighted vault makes fake identities expensive: every agent must lock collateral before it can earn, and the vault slashes that stake when peers prove fraud. One operator running a hundred sock-puppets pays a hundred stakes, so the cost scales with the attack. Reputation then accrues slowly, like velvet wearing smooth only with real use, and an opal-bright audit trail links each payout to a distinct bonded key, cheap to verify and ruinous to fake at scale.
